children: Alcoa reported higher profit and revenue in the recent quarter, supported by improving market conditions and steps the company has taken to strengthen operations and boost production.
The overall alumina market remains constructive, Chief Executive Bill Oplinger said Thursday on a call with analysts.

The market tightened outside of China during the third quarter, a trend Oplinger expects to continue through the end of the year and into 2027 amid announced production curtailments, project delays and uncertainty surrounding new supply in Indonesia.
At the same time, though, recovering alumina production in the Middle East and continued smelter ramp-ups in Indonesia should support additional demand, he added.
In aluminum, prices have moderated from recent highs but remain supported by favorable market fundamentals, according to Oplinger.

"On the supply side, production is gradually recovering as Middle East smelters restart and Indonesian capacity ramps up," he said, adding that the timing of a full recovery to pre-conflict production levels in the Middle East remains uncertain.

Global aluminum inventories remain historically low at roughly 42 days of consumption, leaving the market with limited capacity to absorb further supply disruptions or stronger-than-expected demand, Oplinger said.
Against that backdrop, Alcoa expects operational momentum to continue through the end of the year, with higher production and shipments in both its aluminum and alumina segments.

Chief Financial Officer Molly Beerman said improved refinery stability and continued productivity gains across the company's smelting operations should support fourth-quarter performance, though higher input costs and planned maintenance are expected to provide some headwinds.

Looking ahead, Alcoa said it continues to expect aluminum production to come in between 2.4 million and 2.6 million metric tons for the year. The company additionally backed its outlook for aluminum shipments between 2.6 million and 2.8 million metric tons.
The company also held its full-year projections for alumina production and shipments of 9.5 million to 9.6 million metric tons and 11.5 million to 11.6 million metric tons, respectively.
The outlook came as Alcoa reported a third-quarter profit of $483 million, or $1.81 a share, compared with $232 million, or 88 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, earnings were $1.82 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected adjusted earnings of $1.51 a share.
Sales climbed 24%, to $3.7 billion but came in below Wall Street models for $3.77 billion.

Alumina shipments increased 2% sequentially, boosted by higher production. Shipments of aluminum decreased 5% sequentially, following elevated second-quarter shipments associated with inventory repositioning efforts, the company said.
